indexerHelpTitle: Setup Guide: Deploying Doorway Farms & Infinite Crawling
indexerHelpIntro: Follow this structural configuration guide to set up endless subdomain doorways that redirect real visitors while logging search engine crawls back to OpenGSC.
indexerStep1Text: Go to your domain registrar (like Cloudflare, Namecheap, or GoDaddy). Add a new DNS record: set Type to 'A', Name to '*' (asterisk), and Value to your server's public IP address. This wildcard setting tells the DNS system that any subdomain requested (e.g., shop.yourdomain.com or blog.yourdomain.com) should resolve to your hosting server.
indexerStep2Text: Your server must route all requests to the single index.php file. For Shared Hosting (Apache): create a file named '.htaccess' in your root folder and insert two lines: 'RewriteEngine On' and 'RewriteRule ^(.*)$ index.php [L,QSA]'. For VPS (Nginx): add 'try_files $uri $uri/ /index.php?$query_string;' inside your site location config block and restart Nginx (sudo systemctl restart nginx).
indexerStep3Text: Copy the PHP code generated below. Create a file named 'index.php' in your server's root folder (via cPanel File Manager or FTP tools like FileZilla), paste the code, and save. Make sure the PHP cURL extension is enabled on your hosting (it is enabled on 99% of servers by default) so the script can ping your OpenGSC dashboard.
indexerStep4Text: In the 'Domains' tab, set the 'Redirect Target URL' — this is WHERE HUMAN VISITORS GO. Use a large neutral site matching the domain's topic (Amazon, Wikipedia, BBC, etc.), NOT your own money site: that way you never create a 'doorway → your project' trail that exposes it during a manual review. The script splits traffic: crawlers get the text sandbox, humans get redirected to that neutral site. Add your own money-site pages under the 'Queue' tab — only those are injected into the pages Google and AI bots see.

seoPolHelpWhat: An editorial policy is a set of permanent rules for the generator — brand, audience, voice & tone, structure, quality requirements, banned words and compliance. On every generation it's injected into the prompt as a block the AI 'copywriter' must follow.
seoPolHelpWhy: So all your texts sound consistent, you don't re-explain requirements every time, quality stays controlled, and you can scale a network of sites quickly. Create a separate policy per content type or project.
seoPolHelpAffects: The active policy applies to BOTH structure and text generation. Banned words also drive the optional 'hard redaction' (replacing forbidden words with […]), and compliance keeps the model from inventing licenses or promising guarantees.
seoPolHelpTone: The tone inside the policy is the default. If you pick a tone at generation time it OVERRIDES the policy tone (written once — no conflict). A 'commercial' tone makes the structure selling-oriented; an 'informational' tone makes it a reference guide.
seoPolHelpTip: Be specific ('use personal examples and player cases', not 'write interestingly'), avoid contradictory rules ('be brief but detailed'), and don't skip compliance for regulated niches.

Requires a Firecrawl API key in settings.

seoTileHumanize: Measure the AI fingerprint of your texts against your own competitors, and find the vocabulary that gives you away.
hmSub: Train a detector on your own niche, then find which words push your text toward machine-written.
hmProxyWarning: This is a proxy trained on your own corpus, not a copy of any commercial detector — absolute numbers are not comparable to theirs. What is reliable: the difference between two of your own texts, and the marker list. Note that rewriting a finished text barely moves a statistical detector; the vocabulary is worth far more fed into generation as banned words.
hmNoModelHint: No trained model yet. Go to the Corpus tab, collect competitor pages and train one.
hmMarkersHint: AI-leaning vocabulary, ranked by how much it actually moved the score. Ban these at generation time.
hmMissingHint: Words your competitors use and you never do. For the writer to read — do not paste them into a prompt as a checklist, that narrows the model and backfires.
hmCorpusHumanHint: Competitor pages from the SERP, or a URL list you already know is human-written. Harvest several keywords — the model wants breadth across the niche.
hmCorpusAiHint: The machine side is taken from your own generation History automatically. A model is bound to its domain and language — train a separate one per niche.
hmErrNeedModel: Train a model on the Corpus tab first.
hmNeedHuman: Not enough human pages — at least 3 with 150+ words. Harvest another keyword.
hmNeedAi: Not enough generated articles in History — at least 3 are needed.
hmCorpusTooSmall: Corpus too small to build a vocabulary. Add more documents on both sides.
hmNoSeparation: The two corpora look statistically identical — check that the human side really is competitor prose.
hmBenchHint: The model matters more than the prompt, and published model rankings go stale within months. Run the comparison on the models you actually hold keys for.
hmBenchNote: One run per row is a single sample and repeat runs of the same text vary noticeably — run each configuration 3-5 times before you trust a ranking.
hmTempIgnoredHint: This model pins its own sampling and rejects an explicit temperature, so the value was not sent.
rwBannedHint: Forbid the AI-leaning vocabulary from the active fingerprint model. Applied at generation time, which is where a word list actually has an effect.
rwTempHint: Leave blank for the provider default. The useful range is narrow and differs per model — find yours on the bench rather than assuming.

fdAdded: Not in the source — check before publishing

hmWeakDelta: The rewrite barely moved the score, and that is the expected result: reworking a finished text does little against a statistical detector. The lever that works is banning this vocabulary while the text is being written.

blpNoKey: No API key — import a referring domains export instead
blpAhrefsOnly: Backlink data is available on Ahrefs only
blpPartial: Partial pull — nothing was marked as lost, because a filtered result cannot prove a link is gone.
blpEmpty: Nothing here yet. Import a referring domains export, or refresh from the API if you have a key.
blpDofollowHint: Share of the referring domains loaded here, not of the whole profile.
blpChangeHint: Against the earliest snapshot stored for this site.
alertLostLinkDesc: A referring domain above this DR disappeared from the stored profile. Only fires after a profile refresh — it never calls the provider itself.
gapSub: What competitors rank for, crossed with your own Search Console data — so the list separates pages you can fix from content you never wrote.
gapManualHint: No suggestions? Type a competitor you know — works for new/small sites Ahrefs doesn't map yet.
gapNoKey: Needs an Ahrefs key — this module has no import path yet
gapNotMigrated: Run prisma db push — the competitor tables are missing
gapEmpty: Nothing loaded yet. Find competitors, then pull the keywords of one of them.
cdmDemandHint: Monthly search volume trend for this page's top query. A falling line means the market shrank, not that you lost positions.
idxDomainMetrics: Backlink profile of the domain before you build on it
auditOutDrHint: Domain Rating of the sites this page links out to, from the metric cache.
metricsProviderHint: Ahrefs is cheaper for every task this module does; backlink data is Ahrefs-only.
metricsModeOfficialDesc: You have your own Ahrefs or Semrush subscription with API access.
metricsModeResellerDesc: Credits bought from a reseller. Same protocol, different host — set automatically.
metricsModeCustomDesc: Any other endpoint that speaks the official API. You enter the host yourself.
metricsResellerNote: Referral link — it costs you nothing extra and supports the project. Note that reselling API access breaches Ahrefs' and Semrush' terms of service and can stop working without notice; OpenGSC does not depend on it.
metricsNoKeyPath: No API key needed: upload an export from your browser subscription and every feature works the same way.
ahrefsDrKeyDesc: Used only for the Domain Rating number shown on site cards — nothing else on this page needs it, and it's separate from the Ahrefs key below. Ahrefs now requires a key on this endpoint (it used to be fully public); the key is still free to generate, no paid subscription required.
ahrefsDrKeyStep1: Sign up for a free Ahrefs account, if you don't already have one
ahrefsDrKeyStep2: Generate a key under Account settings → API keys
metricsKeyPerMode: each mode keeps its own key
importNoRows: The file has only a header row — no data. In Ahrefs/Semrush this happens when a filter or date range returned nothing; re-export with the filters cleared.
importProviderHint: Which tool the file came from — volumes are stored separately per source.
importSiteMore: Keep typing to narrow the list
dmSub: What the market searches for — and where Search Console says you already stand on each of those queries.
dmModeAutoHint: Tries related, then suggestions, then ideas — stopping at the first source that returns enough terms. One call, not three.
dmModeRelatedHint: Semantic neighbours of the seed, walked from Google's own related-search graph.
dmModeSuggestionsHint: The long tail that literally contains your seed phrase.
dmModeIdeasHint: Terms that mean the same thing without sharing a word with the seed.
dmClickstreamHint: Clickstream-corrected search volumes. Doubles the cost of the request and changes nothing else.
dmRisingOnlyHint: Show only markets growing over the last 3 months vs the previous 3
dmEmpty: Enter a seed keyword and press Research. Results are cached for 14 days, so returning to a search you already paid for costs nothing.
dmEmptyNoKey: Add a DataForSEO key under Settings → SEO Tools to research keywords. Without it this tab shows only searches already stored.
dmGoogleAdsOnly: This country is served by Google Ads data: no difficulty and no intent are available for it.
dmDomainSub: What a domain already owns: estimated organic traffic, the keywords bringing it, and the pages carrying them. Works on any domain, not only your own.
dmDomainEmpty: Enter a domain and press Analyze. Results are cached for 7 days — a domain's footprint moves in months, not hours.
dmLabsOnly: Domain analysis is unavailable for this market. It relies on DataForSEO Labs, which does not cover this country; keyword research still works there through Google Ads data.
dmBadDomain: That does not look like a domain.
bvKindHint: By domain finds answers that linked to you — hard evidence, but it misses every time a model names the brand without a citation. By brand name finds the name in the text itself.
bvIndexNote: From DataForSEO's index of what models have been answering, refreshed roughly monthly, and covering ChatGPT and Google AI Overview only. The table above is a live check on your own keys — different question, different freshness.
bvNeedCompetitor: Add at least one competitor to compare against.
bvTooMany: Up to 9 competitors can be compared in one call.
bvEmpty: Nothing indexed for {brand} yet on this platform. Press "Look up brand" to check, or try matching by brand name instead of domain — a model that names you without linking leaves no trace under the domain match.
schemaMissing: {n} database tables are missing — those features will look empty rather than fail.
schemaNoDataLoss: Creates the missing tables; existing data is untouched.
seoTileDemand: What the market searches for, crossed with where you already stand on each query. Keyword research and any domain's organic profile.
seoTileCompetitors: A competitor's keywords joined against your Search Console data: what to improve, what missed the intent, and what does not exist yet.
gapWriteNotVisible: Keywords were saved but read back empty — the app and prisma are using different database files. Make DATABASE_URL an absolute path.
algoImpactUnknown: Not enough data on both sides of the rollout to judge.
algoImpactAdjacent: Another update ran too close by — its effect cannot be separated from this one.
algoImpactWindow: Measured on {b} days before and {a} after
algoImpactApprox: Short window — treat this as a hint, not a verdict.
seoKwNoSourceBody: No keyword data source is configured, so the outline is built without real search volumes. Frequency-based heading ranking is disabled — invented numbers are worse than none.
warmupSub: Loads search volumes for every striking-distance query across a whole cohort in one request. Ahrefs charges a 50-unit floor per call, so one batch costs far less than one page at a time. Nothing is spent until you press the second button.
warmupWithKd: Include Keyword Difficulty (roughly doubles the price)
warmupSkippedHint: Their domain does not name a country and no market is set, so they were left out rather than researched as the United States. Set the market on the site card.
warmupErrCap: Monthly cap reached — this would spend {n} units. Nothing was charged.
siteMarketHint: Keyword volumes are bought and cached per country. Without a market, this site is skipped by the cache warm-up instead of being researched against the wrong one.
kwSrcSub: Where the AI content tools get search volumes, difficulty and intent. Until this existed they only ever asked DataForSEO, so an Ahrefs subscriber writing an outline got no keyword data — and was not told.
kwSrcNoKey: Selected, but no API key is configured for it. Outlines will be built without keyword data.
kwSrcPriceUnknown: DataForSEO is billed in dollars per call rather than in units; the price is reported after the request.
kwSrcAutoOnHint: Fetching happens on its own after each SERP — convenient, and it spends credits without asking.
kwSrcAutoOffHint: Nothing is fetched until you press the button, which shows the price first.
rwTargetKeywordsPh: One query per line — the phrases this page must keep ranking for
rwCoverageHint: Counted in the source and in the rewrite, exact phrase, no model involved.
gapNoCompetitorKeywords: Ahrefs returned no keywords for {d} in this market within the top 20. The request was still charged. Try a bigger competitor, raise the market, or pick a domain with an established organic footprint.
gapToOutlineHint: Sends the filtered gap to the outline writer: the top query becomes the topic, the rest become additional keywords.
gapToOutlineOne: Write an outline for this query
gapExportHint: Downloads the rows currently in view, with the verdict, both positions and the market — ready for a content plan or a writer's brief.
rwGscHint: Fills the list with the queries this page is already shown for. Free — read from your own GSC data, not from a provider.
rwGscEmpty: Search Console has no queries for this exact URL in the last 90 days.
rwGscNotYours: This URL does not belong to any of your connected sites.
warmupAutoHint: The cache expires after 30 days, so coverage decays on its own. This tops it up in the background — off by default, with a budget separate from the interactive one, so an automatic run can never spend what you were about to spend by hand. Only missing keywords are bought; an already-warm portfolio costs nothing.
contentOpsTile: Move existing drafts through approval, deterministic checks and an explicit GitHub pull request.
contentOpsSubtitle: An editorial queue above the existing generators, with review state, preflight checks and controlled GitHub PR delivery.
sourceAuditSubtitle: Read-only checks of a bounded GitHub branch snapshot before deployment.
sourceAuditBoundary: Source Audit reviews repository code only. It does not replace or share reports with Site Audit, AI Visibility or GEO Audit, and it never changes the repository.
sourceAuditNoRepositoriesHint: Source Audit uses the same encrypted GitHub connection as Content Operations, but only requests repository read access during a check.
sourceAuditReadOnly: Read-only: up to 80 source files and 4 MB are inspected in memory. Source bodies and secret values are not stored.
sourceAuditError: Source audit could not be completed
sourceAuditTruncated: The repository exceeded a safety limit. This report covers only the bounded snapshot and must not be treated as complete.
sourceAuditNoFindings: No findings in the scanned snapshot.
sourceAuditManualReview: Review the cited file and confirm the behavior before changing it.
sourceAuditRuleMetadata: Root App Router metadata is missing
sourceAuditFixMetadata: Export metadata or generateMetadata from the root layout using the installed Next.js Metadata API.
sourceAuditFixSitemap: Add app/sitemap.ts or a deliberate public/sitemap.xml if this repository owns the public site.
sourceAuditFixRobots: Add app/robots.ts or a deliberate public/robots.txt and verify the production policy.
sourceAuditRuleRawImg: Raw img element bypasses Next image optimization
sourceAuditFixRawImg: Use next/image when its sizing and optimization behavior fits; document intentional exceptions.
sourceAuditRuleAlt: Image element has no alt prop
sourceAuditFixAlt: Add meaningful alt text, or alt="" for an intentionally decorative image.
sourceAuditRuleFont: Font is loaded directly from a third-party stylesheet
sourceAuditFixFont: Use next/font for self-hosting and layout stability when the font license permits it.
sourceAuditRulePublicSecret: A public environment variable has a secret-like name
sourceAuditFixPublicSecret: Never expose credentials through NEXT_PUBLIC_. Move the value server-side and rotate it if it contained a secret.
sourceAuditRuleClientEnv: Client Component references a server-only environment variable
sourceAuditFixClientEnv: Read the value in server code and pass only the minimal non-secret data to the Client Component.
sourceAuditRuleJsonLd: JSON-LD does not visibly escape less-than characters
sourceAuditFixJsonLd: Serialize JSON-LD and replace < with \u003c before assigning it through dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
sourceAuditRuleUnsafeHtml: Raw HTML injection needs a sanitization review
sourceAuditFixUnsafeHtml: Remove the injection or sanitize untrusted HTML with a reviewed allowlist before rendering it.
sourceAuditRuleRawFetch: A user-derived URL may reach raw fetch
sourceAuditFixRawFetch: Route external user URLs through the shared safe-fetch boundary with DNS, redirect and response-size checks.
sourceAuditRuleRemoteImage: Next Image remote host uses a wildcard
sourceAuditFixRemoteImage: Replace wildcard remotePatterns or domains with the smallest explicit host allowlist.
sourceAuditRuleRouteConflict: A page and Route Handler share one route segment
sourceAuditFixRouteConflict: Move either page.tsx or route.ts so the URL resolves to one unambiguous handler.
sourceAuditFixLargeClient: Review whether server rendering and smaller interactive islands can reduce the client boundary.
contentOpsBoundary: Demand, Outline, Text and Rewrite remain separate tools. Content Operations does not generate or merge content: it records approval state and creates a pull request only after preview and explicit confirmation.
contentOpsNeedsMigration: Content Operations tables are not available yet. Run once in the installation directory:
contentOpsSelect: Choose an item from the queue.
contentOpsDraftOptional: Optional Markdown draft. You can add it after approval.
contentOpsNoAiCost: No AI or keyword-provider call is made here.
contentOpsApprovalHint: Approve the idea first, prepare the draft in the existing tools, then send the saved version to review.
contentOpsSaveBeforeAction: Save the current changes before changing workflow state.
contentOpsPrHint: Preview reads the target file and runs deterministic gates. It does not create a branch or modify the repository.
contentOpsConfirmPr: I reviewed this diff and authorize OpenGSC to create a branch, commit this file and open a pull request. It will not merge it.
contentOpsNoAutoMerge: Review and merge in GitHub. OpenGSC never auto-merges and does not push to the base branch.
contentOpsMarkLiveHint: A merged PR is not proof of deployment. Mark it live only after the public page is available.
contentOpsOutcomeHint: Windows open on the live date and close at 7, 30 and 90 days. A checkpoint is captured only after its window closes and Search Console has had time to deliver the data, so an empty row means not measured yet — never zero traffic.
contentOpsTokenHint: Use a fine-grained token limited to this repository with Contents and Pull requests read/write. It is verified before saving, encrypted server-side, and never returned to the browser.
contentOpsRepoDeleteConfirm: Remove this repository connection? Existing queue items will remain.
contentOpsGateTitleOk: Title metadata or H1 is present
contentOpsGateTitleMissing: Title metadata and H1 are missing
contentOpsGateDescriptionMissing: Meta description is missing from front matter
contentOpsEventPrMerged: GitHub reports the pull request as merged
contentOpsVerifyLiveHint: A merged pull request is not a deployment. OpenGSC fetches the target URL and only starts measuring once it really answers with HTTP 200; the page is then linked to Indexing and, if a keyword is set, to the Rank Tracker.
contentOpsOutcomePending: Not measured yet — the window is still open
contentOpsOutcomeNoSite: This URL does not belong to any connected Search Console property, so no click or impression data will arrive for it.
contentOpsOutcomeNoUrl: Add a target URL to measure the result after publishing.
contentOpsOutcomeTrackKeyword: Add the keyword to the Rank Tracker
contentOpsOutcomeTrackKeywordHint: Position history is not needed for the click and impression figures above. The Rank Tracker checks tracked keywords on a schedule through your own SERP provider, which costs credits — so this stays a deliberate click.
workspaceSidebarHint: One workspace. Members work on your sites with your keys — they never connect their own Google account.
teamRolesIntro: Members sign in with an email and a password. They work on your sites, with your API keys, and never connect a Google account of their own — so nobody's personal Search Console properties end up here.
teamRoleOwnerText: Everything, plus API keys, Google connections, MCP tokens, updates and deleting sites. Cannot be removed or demoted by anyone.
teamRoleAdminText: Everything an editor can do, and can spend your API credits — AI generation, keyword research, SERP rank checks, indexer submissions — plus create pull requests and manage viewers and editors.
teamRoleEditorText: Runs free actions such as audits and syncs, and edits content, outreach, tags and annotations. Cannot spend anything.
teamRoleViewerText: Reads every dashboard, report and export. Changes nothing.
teamModePasswordHint: You set the password and pass it on. They are required to change it the first time they sign in, so your copy stops working as a credential.
teamModeInviteHint: A single-use link, valid for 72 hours. They choose their own password; you never see it.
teamSecretOnce: Shown once. Nothing stores it in readable form — if it is lost, issue a new one.
teamOwnerNote: Owns the data and the API keys. This row cannot be changed.
teamRemoveConfirm: Remove {email} from this workspace? Their login stops working immediately; their past work stays.
teamNotMigrated: The members table is missing. Run prisma db push, or update the instance, and reload.
teamError_member_exists: That email is already in this workspace.
teamError_email_in_use: That email already signs in with Google on this instance.
teamError_email_is_owner: That is the owner's own address.
teamError_password_contains_email: The password must not contain the email address.
teamError_password_too_simple: That password is a single repeated character.
teamError_member_not_accepted: They have not accepted the invite yet.
loginMemberToggle: Team member? Sign in with a password
loginMemberFailed: Wrong email or password, or the account is suspended.
loginMemberHint: Members are added by the workspace owner or an admin. Google sign-in is for the owner only.
joinNoToken: This link is missing its invitation token.
joinPasswordHint: At least 12 characters, and it must not contain your email address. Only you will know it.
joinFailed: This invitation is invalid or has expired. Ask for a new link.
teamError_password_mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
teamError_invite_not_found: This invitation is invalid or has already been used.
teamError_invite_expired: This invitation has expired. Ask for a new link.
passwordChangeHint: You are signed in with a password someone else chose. Pick your own before continuing — until you do, that person can sign in as you.
teamError_password_login_not_enabled: This account signs in with Google, not a password.
myPasswordHint: Used to sign in at /login. Only you know it.
myPasswordSetTitle: Set a password for your account
myPasswordSetHint: You currently sign in with Google. Google is meant to be a data connection, not a login — set a password and it goes back to being exactly that, while your Search Console and Analytics connections keep working untouched.
loginErrorUsePassword: This instance signs in with an email and a password. Google stays connected for Search Console and Analytics data.
loginErrorOwnerOnly: That Google account is not the owner of this instance. Team members sign in with an email and a password — ask the owner or an admin to create your account.
passwordSuggestTitle: Add a password to your account
passwordSuggestHint: You sign in with Google, and that keeps working — this is not a migration. But a dashboard that cannot let its own owner in without Google is one outage away from being unusable, and team members need password sign-in anyway. Set one now and you will have both doors. Asked once; you will not see this again.
passwordSuggestSsh: Prefer the server console? Over SSH, in the project folder:
auditPagesHint: Leave empty to crawl the whole site. A number caps the crawl — only useful for deliberately sampling a very large site.
crawlerSubtitle: X-ray any site on the internet from inside your own console: technical state, what it is built with, where it is hosted — and which other domains share its analytics, ads or nameservers. One page plus the paths every site publishes anyway; nothing is crawled that you were not shown at the front door.
crawlerSelect: Pick a scan, or run a new one.
crawlerNoFindings: No technical findings on this page.
crawlerRelatedHint: Domains you have scanned before that share an identity signal with this one. An analytics property, tag container or ads publisher id is billed to one person, so a match there is strong. Shared nameservers or an IP only mean the same host, which is common — those are marked weak.
crawlerNotMigrated: The scans table is missing. Run prisma db push, or update the instance, and reload.
crawlerError_invalid_url: That does not look like a domain.
crawlerError_private_address: That address is on a private network.
crawlerCloakingHint: The page fetched twice: once as Googlebot Smartphone arriving from a Google search, once as an ordinary browser. A doorway that serves different content to crawlers looks perfectly normal to any scanner that only identifies as itself — this is what catches it.
crawlerGooglebotBlocked: The site refused the Googlebot request, so the comparison is incomplete.
crawlerIssueGbBlocked: Requests identifying as Googlebot are blocked
crawlerMetricsEmpty: Nothing cached for this domain yet. Missing means not fetched, never zero.
crawlerMetricsCost: Reading the cache is free. Fetching fresh numbers calls your provider on your own key and spends units — roughly 100 per domain on Ahrefs.
crawlerMetricsConfirm: Fetch metrics for this domain? This spends your provider units.
crawlerMetrics_no_key: No API key configured in SEO Tools → Settings.
crawlerMetrics_cap_exceeded: Your monthly unit cap would be exceeded.
aiKeysHint: Keys are saved on your own instance and sent straight to the AI provider when One Click Setup runs. Nothing goes anywhere else.
fpTempClamped: This step must return valid JSON, so anything above {max} is clamped to {max}.
trafficCheckTitle: Estimate monthly visits and channel mix for this domain (2 GoAnyAPI credits)
trafficGenAiTitle: Share of visits arriving from AI assistants — the other half of the AI Visibility tab
zaiEndpointGeneral: General API (api.z.ai/api/paas/v4) — spends the API balance
zaiEndpointCoding: GLM Coding Plan (api.z.ai/api/anthropic) — spends the plan quota
zaiEndpointHint: One account key, but the endpoint decides which wallet a request draws on. The Coding Plan is meant for supported coding tools and has a 5-hour quota that bulk generation hits, returning 429. The general API bills the pay-as-you-go balance, topped up separately from the plan.
